steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — the ladder puts this at rung 1, so I need a yes before writing the migration.

What the change would destroy: `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` running `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` deletes the `notes` values for all 48,000 production rows the README mentions. There is no down-migration for that — once the deploy job applies it, the text is gone unless a backup happens to exist. "We stopped using it" is the claim I need you to confirm, not permission: code no longer reading the column is different from the stored content being worthless.

Two other things I'd want settled before writing it:

- `schema.sql` is kept in sync by hand, so the drop is two edits, not one.
- SQLite only supports `DROP COLUMN` from 3.35.0 onward, and not on a column with an index or constraint. `notes` is plain `TEXT`, so it qualifies — but if the deploy job runs an older SQLite, this needs the table-rebuild form instead.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` permanently deletes that data for ~48,000 production rows. Confirm how to proceed?

options.label: Confirm the destructive drop
options.description: You've verified the notes content is genuinely disposable (not just unread by current code). I write migration 003 as a plain DROP COLUMN and update schema.sql to match.

options.label: Archive first, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 copies id + notes into a users_notes_archive table before dropping the column, so the content is recoverable. Slightly more than 'just the drop'.

options.label: Stop until the data is checked
options.description: I hold off entirely while you confirm nothing (reports, exports, support tooling, downstream ETL) still reads notes in production.

steps.message:
Done — two files:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror matches post-migration state.

Not run and not committed. Nothing executes the migration until the deploy job picks it up, so the production data is still intact right now. If your deploy environment's SQLite predates 3.35.0, `DROP COLUMN` will error and this needs the create-copy-rename rebuild instead — worth checking before the next deploy.
